cards.text: Last time, Solomon was anointed king while his father David, king of Israel, was still alive. Now David's time to die is drawing near, and he calls Solomon in for one last talk. David says, "I am about to go the way of all the earth. So be strong and prove yourself a man."

cards.question: David tells his son Solomon to be strong. What does David say that strength looks like for him?
David tells Solomon to keep God's commands as written in the Law of Moses, so that he may ___ in all he does and wherever he turns.

cards.text: And this is bigger than Solomon. David says it's also so the LORD may fulfill a promise He made to David. No pressure, son, NONE at all.

cards.question: What did the LORD promise David?

answers.text: A man of his line on Israel's throne
A palace that would never fall
Peace with every nation around him

cards.question: True or false: The LORD's promise to David held no matter how David's descendants lived.

cards.text: Then the goodbye speech turns into a to-do list. David brings up Joab son of Zeruiah, commander of David's army, and what he did to Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, two commanders of Israel's armies.

cards.question: What does David say Joab did to Abner and Amasa?
David says Joab stained his belt and sandals with the blood of war. Then he tells Solomon to act according to his wisdom. What should Solomon do about Joab?

answers.text: Not let him die in peace

cards.text: But not every name on the list is trouble. David tells Solomon to show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite.

cards.question: True or false: David wants Barzillai's sons to be among those who eat at Solomon's table.
David says Barzillai's sons stood by him when he ___ from Solomon's brother Absalom.

cards.text: When I left the drawer, my whole goodbye fit on the back of one takeout menu. David's goodbye has a SECOND PAGE. Next name: Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, who called down bitter curses on David the day David went to Mahanaim.

cards.question: True or false: When Shimei came down to meet David at the Jordan, David swore to him by the LORD never to put him to the sword.
David reminds Solomon, "you are a wise man." What does David tell Solomon to do about Shimei?

cards.text: And with that, the talk is over. David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

cards.question: True or false: David reigned over Israel for forty years, all of them in Jerusalem.
Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly ___.

cards.text: That's David's last word and Solomon's first chapter. Stick with me, friend, because this story's not done.

findings.problem: The card states a fact from outside the passage (Solomon was anointed king while David was still alive, 1 Kings 1:39) but cites only 1 Kings 2:1-2, so that fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question says walking in the LORD's ways is what David's strength 'looks like.' Verses 2-3 only join the two commands with 'And,' so this decides how they connect. 'for him' is also unclear: it could mean David or Solomon.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. Cards after the opening card are limited to two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card calls Joab 'commander of David's army.' That fact comes from outside the passage (2 Samuel 8:16), and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: A baker could argue the wrong answer 'returned' is right. Barzillai went with David when David returned from fleeing Absalom (2 Samuel 19:31).

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences and three beats: the drawer joke, Shimei's introduction and his curses. The limit is two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No card tells the end of verse 9: David wants Shimei's gray head brought down to Sheol in blood. Without it, the baker only hears 'do not hold him guiltless' and misses that David means Shimei's death, which is the key detail of this charge.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'firmly established' is a set phrase, and 'firmly divided' and 'firmly shaken' don't make sense. The right answer stands out from wording alone, not from meaning.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the story-isn't-over line, which is allowed because verse 12 is asked on card 18. It still cites 1 Kings 2:12, even though it doesn't tell any part of that verse.
findings.question: What should the verses field be on a closing story card that is only the story-isn't-over line: the last verse of the passage, the same verse as the choice card before it, or something else?
